clue.text: Task force combining business with pleasure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a committee set up to look into a particular question
second meaning, read literally: a job plus a celebration

explanation.surface: A committee whose members manage to enjoy themselves while doing their official duties.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the phrase taken word by word: WORKING is business, PARTY is pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A working party is a group appointed to investigate and report on a matter, much the same thing as a task force.

clue.text: Hostile sides one encountered in vigil

indicators.note: what is encountered in a place is found inside it, so these letters sit within the vigil

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept over the dead
right and left are the two sides
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Opposing factions meet during an all-night watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Warlike means aggressive or ready to fight, an adjective for an attitude of enmity like hostile.

clue.text: Clarinets, poles apart, ruined musical performance

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so what remains is jumbled into a new order
the poles go apart, departing from the word they were in

parts.note: taken as written
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Woodwind players at odds with each other spoil a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles apart' suggests the clarinettists disagree, but it asks for N and S to leave the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert given by a soloist or small group, a kind of musical performance.

clue.text: Medical specialist needs to confine one's patient, finally

parts.note: to intern is to imprison, especially in wartime
I for one, then the 's

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the preceding word, so only its closing letter counts

parts.note: the last letter of patient

explanation.surface: A doctor has to keep his patient in the ward until the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage an internist is a physician of internal medicine; 'patient' is not a person here but a source of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An internist is a physician specialising in diseases of the internal organs, so a medical specialist.

clue.text: Enormous soldier — a six-footer

parts.note: a GI is an American private soldier
an insect has six feet, and an ant is one example

explanation.surface: A huge soldier standing six feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' reads as a tall man; here it is an insect, which has six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant is used as an adjective meaning huge or of great size, the same sense as enormous.

clue.text: Dispose of lots you reportedly carried in case

indicators.note: something carried in a case is held inside it

parts.note: a legal case is an action

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word you is taken by its sound

parts.note: the letter name sounds like you

explanation.surface: Someone said you carried a great deal of something in your suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like luggage but is a lawsuit, an action in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To auction goods is to sell them in lots to the highest bidder, a way of disposing of lots.

clue.text: Port with more noticeable aftertaste

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Moroccan harbour city on the Strait of Gibraltar
second meaning: the comparative of tangy

explanation.surface: A glass of port that leaves a stronger taste in the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Port suggests the fortified wine, which fits the tasting surface, but it is the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is the Moroccan seaport, and as a comparative adjective it means sharper or more pungent in flavour.

clue.text: Cutting remark one was going to make

definitions.text: Cutting remark one was going to make

parts.words: Cutting remark one was going to make
parts.note: surface reading: a barbed comment someone intended to say but did not
setter's reading: the remark made while one was going, a parting shot fired while leaving

explanation.surface: A wounding comment someone meant to say but held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was going to' reads as 'intended to'; it actually means 'while departing'. Parthian horse archers shot backwards while retreating.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a sharp final remark delivered while leaving, after the mounted archers of ancient Parthia who fired while riding away.

clue.text: Fruit-tree put in bed after start of month

indicators.note: after places the bed second, following the opening of the month

parts.note: the opening letters of April, a month
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a young fruit tree in a flower bed early in the month.
explanation.walkthrough: The month must be guessed: only April's first four letters fit, and the bed comes after them.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small stone-fruit tree, Prunus armeniaca, grown for its orange fruit.

clue.text: Emphasizes it's what a dollar's worth

parts.note: taken as written
a dollar is worth C (the Roman hundred) cents

explanation.surface: A remark about the value of an American dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so 'a hundred cents' becomes A C CENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To accent a syllable or point is to stress it, so accents is a verb meaning stresses or highlights.

clue.text: Dedicated as a batsman on 99, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wholly committed to one aim
second meaning, read literally: a cricketer one run short of a century has his mind on a single run

explanation.surface: A determined cricketer just one short of a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a single is one run, and 100 runs (a century) is a landmark, so a batsman on 99 is thinking only of one more.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-minded means devoted to one purpose with full determination, as a committed or dedicated person is.

clue.text: He does all he can to entangle queen

parts.note: to twist threads together is to entangle them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A man tries every trick to ensnare a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is not the verb of effort but 'cheats', as in 'he did me out of a fiver'; a twister is a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a dishonest person who cheats others, someone who 'does' every victim he possibly can.

clue.text: Teacher's fee may be worked out in it

indicators.note: material that is worked is kneaded and shaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three short words together supply the seven letters

explanation.surface: A teacher's charges might be calculated as part of the lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to read 'worked out' as calculated; the indicator is 'worked' alone, and 'out' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition means teaching, and also the fee charged for it, as in tuition fees paid to a school or tutor.

clue.text: A businessman's profession is perfectly suitable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a trader professes

explanation.surface: Commerce is said to be the perfect career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profession' means a declaration, not a career: the businessman announces I DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something that is the best possible fit for a purpose, perfectly suitable.

clue.text: Modish leader, as a rule

parts.note: what is in is fashionable
a general leads an army

explanation.surface: A fashionable commander, as is usually the case.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or for the most part, the same sense as the idiom given.

clue.text: Ancient Mariner, for example — or what he had to face

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old man, as Coleridge's mariner is called a ... loon
second meaning: the whiskers covering an old man's face

explanation.surface: Coleridge's old sailor and the ordeal that lay ahead of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had to face' suggests an ordeal at sea; it means what grew on his face.
explanation.definitionFit: A greybeard is an old man, and the Ancient Mariner is one; literally it is the grey whiskers an old man's chin carries.

clue.text: Modern Englishman's home city

parts.note: modern means new
from the saying 'an Englishman's home is his castle'

explanation.surface: A newly built house in the town where an Englishman lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle upon Tyne is a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle is a major English city on the River Tyne, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Squire's picture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Squire ..., the hard-drinking landowner in Fielding's Tom Jones

explanation.walkthrough: Picture is used in the old sense of a film or movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Western is the surname of Fielding's fox-hunting squire, and also a film genre set in the American frontier.

clue.text: Alarming a partnership about merger

parts.note: taken as written
a couple, joined together, speak of themselves as we
some means roughly, as in some twenty people
surface padding, perhaps hinting that the partners merge into one pronoun

explanation.surface: A frightening proposal to merge two partners' businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merger' has no clear role: perhaps it says the partners merge into WE; the parse is loose, but the crossings confirm the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome originally meant inspiring awe or dread, so something awesome can be frightening or alarming.

clue.text: Energy shown by second eleven, say

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
an eleven is one example of a side, in cricket or football

explanation.surface: The reserve side shows plenty of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' reads as a reserve side, but the two words split: second gives one letter, eleven a whole side.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is used figuratively for vigour or drive, as in running out of steam or letting off steam.

clue.text: Medical expert's son succeeds bishop of 23

indicators.note: to succeed someone is to take their place, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for son
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the answer to 23 across

explanation.surface: A doctor's son follows the local bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the answer to 23 across and let the son's letter take the bishop's place at its start.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor who operates, an expert in one branch of medicine.

clue.text: A precious possession, this little woolly jumper?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from Nathan's parable in 2 Samuel 12, a poor man's one treasured thing
second meaning: a young female sheep that skips about

explanation.surface: A treasured hand-knitted pullover for a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a jumper is a sweater; here it is a creature that jumps, a frisky young sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: One's ewe lamb is one's dearest possession, after the biblical parable; literally it is a young female sheep.

clue.text: Weird banshee a shadow of her former self?

definitions.text: a shadow of her former self

indicators.note: something weird is strange and out of its normal shape, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wailing Irish spirit that has faded into a ghost of what it was.
explanation.walkthrough: A banshee is a female spirit of Irish folklore whose wail foretells a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person whose fame or ability has faded, someone now only a shadow of what they once were.

clue.text: Composition I found amongst religious books

indicators.note: something found amongst others sits within them, so it goes inside

parts.note: NT is the New Testament
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A writer says they discovered something among sacred texts.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece of music written for nine instruments or voices, a kind of composition.

clue.text: Flourish black spur

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to spur on is to urge on

explanation.surface: A dark spur, as worn by a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow or develop rapidly, to thrive, the same as to flourish.

clue.text: Place restrictions on game with county

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
Down is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Restrictions are imposed on a county's sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a cup tie is a knockout match; County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie someone down is to limit their freedom or commit them firmly, which is restricting them.

clue.text: It's normal, say, to mature

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
wine and cheese age as they mature

explanation.surface: Growing up is said to be a perfectly normal process.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes what is typical or ordinary, the usual standard, so it matches normal as an adjective.

clue.text: Worker at last upset one with lower-class bias

parts.note: turned upside down
snob is an old word for a shoemaker, who works at a last, the foot-shaped block

explanation.surface: A worker who finally lost their temper with someone prejudiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' looks like 'finally', but a last is a cobbler's foot-shaped form, and snob originally meant a cobbler.
explanation.definitionFit: An inverted snob scorns upper-class taste and admires working-class ways, a prejudice in favour of the lower classes.
